newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Cofinec returns to profit in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Cofinec returns to profit in Q1 '97.

text.p: French-registered packaging company Cofinec, which released its first quarter earnings report on Thursday, said it returned to profit after three quarters of net losses.
"The corrective measures implemented in the second half of 1996 have begun to show positive results," Alois Manich, President of the management board said in Cofinec's earnings report.
"Although this is an encouraging trend, the company believes that the full impact of these measures will not be realised until the second half of 1997," he said.

The company, which operates in Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, reported an IAS net profit of three million French francs for the first three months, down from a net profit of 4.7 million in Q1 1996.

Its operating profit for the January-March period amounted to 11.7 million French francs, higher than in the preceeding three quarters, but 26.1 percent below the Q1 1996 result of 15.8 million francs.
"The decrease in the operating result compared to one year ago is primarily attributable to the start-up costs of Cofinec Polska," the report said.

"Gross margins, which began to decline in Q2 1996, have continued to recover steadily during this quarter." Gross margins improved to 21.4 percent from 18.7 percent in the last quarter of 1996 and 16.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
The company said it retained its market share and boosted production and sales despite the increased competition which impacted sales prices and margins in 1996.
"Total production volume in Q1 1997 was 12,545 tonnes, exceeding the quarterly production volume of all four quarters of last year."
